description:
Declare numeric stats on threads, log values, and show them over time. To track an event, declare an int stat and log 1 each time it happens: with --agg sum the series counts occurrences, with --agg max it shows whether it happened at all.

Subcommands:
  new NAME --thread THREAD --type int|decimal --agg sum|last|max — declare a stat in the thread file's frontmatter
  list [--json] — list declared stats
  log NAME VALUE [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] — add a value to buffer.md
  series NAME [--by day|week|month] [--since DATE] [--until DATE] [--json] — the stat's value per period

Flags:
  new:
    NAME             lowercase letters, digits and '-'; unique across the vault; put a unit in the name if unclear (run-km)
    --thread THREAD  required; thread name, 'Kind/Name' or wikilink
    --type           required; int (whole numbers, counts, events) or decimal
    --agg            required; sum adds a period's values, last takes the latest, max the largest
  log:
    VALUE            whole number for int; plain number such as 12.50 for decimal (never 1e3)
    -d, --date DATE  YYYY-MM-DD (default today)
    -t, --time HH:MM default now
  series:
    --by       day, week or month (default day); weeks start Monday
    --since DATE, --until DATE  inclusive bounds
    --json     JSON output; empty periods are null ('-' in text), not 0

Examples:
  ["new", "pushups", "--thread", "Topics/Fitness", "--type", "int", "--agg", "sum"]
  ["log", "pushups", "25"]
  ["log", "run-km", "5.2", "-d", "2026-10-20"]
  ["series", "pushups", "--by", "week", "--json"]

Notes:
  log only writes to buffer.md. buffer flush files the value in the thread's daily log. series reads both logs and the unflushed buffer.
  There is no rename or delete. To change a declaration, edit the thread frontmatter; values already logged are not rewritten.
  Exit 1 (nothing written): name not declared, declared twice, or already declared (new); value of the wrong type; bad date or time; bad name; thread does not resolve or its frontmatter cannot be extended; a logged value in series has the wrong type; --since after --until.
  Exit 2: usage error (missing argument, unknown --type or --agg).
